title: Healthscore SLI taxonomy and renewal tracker
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc defines the canonical SLI taxonomy we will use in QBRs and renewal conversations, plus a compact per-customer tracker layout that CS can copy into customer-facing trackers. Focus metrics: latency, uptime (availability), cost-per-token, and cache hit rate.

Summary of intent (one-liner):
Make QBR metrics defensible, repeatable, and aligned with engineering SLAs so renewals conversations can focus on business impacts (response time for user flows, cost levers, and reliability improvements).

Audience: customer success managers, solutions engineers, product ops, and on-call SREs who contribute to the QBR metric slides.

Quick definitions (short):
- Latency: p50/p95 response time for inference end-to-end (client request -> final token delivered) measured at Redwood gateway.
- Uptime: % of successful API availability during rolling 30d window, excluding scheduled maintenance windows.
- Cost-per-token: realized infra cost allocated to tokens for the customer's usage window (30d), using committed capacity or shared pool cost model as applicable.
- Cache hit rate: fraction of requests where prefix/KV cache avoided full model compute (cache hits / total requests).

Measurement details (canonical):
1) Latency (canonical):
  - Signal: gateway_latency_ms per request (includes auth + routing + model-serving time + stream overhead).
  - Aggregates: p50, p95, p99 over the reporting window (default 30 days for QBR).
  - Unit: milliseconds.
  - Calculation: take all successful inference requests (status code 2xx) for the customer, compute statistical percentiles.
  - Notes: exclude warmup/probe synthetic requests if flagged; include streaming end-to-end measurement when client uses streaming.
  - Example: p50=120ms, p95=420ms for ChatFlow v1 route. If p95 > target for this customer tier, add a row in the QBR "Action" column recommending batching or higher dedicated capacity.

2) Uptime / availability (canonical):
  - Signal: successful_request_ratio over time. Harvest from telemetry (gateway + model-serving combined).
  - Window: rolling 30d for QBR snapshot; 7d and 90d are presented as context.
  - Calculation: uptime = (successful_requests - allowed_maintenance_failures) / (total_requests - allowed_maintenance_requests) * 100.
  - Definitions: successful_requests = 2xx responses; allowed_maintenance_requests = requests during scheduled maintenance windows documented in maintenance calendar for the customer region.
  - SLA vs SLO: for customers with contractual SLAs we display both SLA number (contract) and observed SLO (measured).
  - Example: 30d observed = 99.97% (3x 5m incidents recorded during window).

3) Cost-per-token (canonical):
  - Purpose: help customer teams understand leading cost levers and show where Redwood Optimize recommendations could reduce spend.
  - Numerator: sum of infra cost allocated to the customer's inference (GPU hours * unit GPU cost + auxiliary infra + networking) in USD for the window. For Dedicated customers, use committed-cost allocation; for shared customers pro-rate by measured token usage and compute time.
  - Denominator: billed input+output tokens for same window.
  - Unit: USD / 1k tokens (we standardize to per-1k tokens in slides).
  - Calculation notes: if customer has reserved capacity, show both (1) realized effective cost-per-token given committed consumption and (2) marginal cost-per-token for burst usage beyond reservation.
  - Example: infra_cost = $7,200 over 30d, tokens = 36M => cost_per_1k = (7200 / 36_000) = $0.20/1k.
  - Actionable levers shown: lower sequence length, enable prefix caching, change to lower-cost quantized model variant, or move hot routes to dedicated pool.

4) Cache hit rate (canonical):
  - Signal: cache_hits divided by cache_eligible_requests. Two subsignals we track: prefix_cache_hit_rate and KV_cache_hit_rate.
  - Definition: cache_eligible_requests = requests where request payload matched configured cache policy (e.g., identical prefix, or memoized embeddings).
  - Calculation: cache_hit_rate = cache_hits / cache_eligible_requests. Report as percentage.
  - Measurement caveats: we must be explicit about what is 'eligible' — if cache policy is conservative, raw hit rate will look low even if useful. Always show both eligible count and hit count to avoid misleading percentages.
  - Example: eligible=12,000 requests, hits=7,800 => hit_rate=65%.

KPI table template (copy into customer tracker, plain text table):
| Metric | Window | Canonical measure | Value | Target for tier | Trend (7d) | Notes / Action |
| Latency p50 | 30d | gateway_latency_ms p50 | 120ms | <=150ms | -5% | Consider prefix cache for login route |
| Latency p95 | 30d | gateway_latency_ms p95 | 420ms | <=350ms | +12% | Investigate batching on search route |
| Uptime | 30d | availability % | 99.97% | >=99.9% | stable | One 5m incident on 2026-01-18 (SRE incident CS-842) |
| Cost / 1k tokens | 30d | infra_cost / tokens * 1000 | $0.20 | $0.18 | +8% | Low utilization of reserved capacity; propose commit adjustment |
| Cache hit rate | 30d | hits / eligible | 65% | >=70% | -3% | Expand cache eligibility for FAQ route (needs config change) |

Tracker usage instructions for CSMs (how to update quickly):
- Pull 30d export from the metrics dashboard (dashboard name: CS QBR metrics — customer view).
- Copy percentile numbers and include a small historical sparkline (we provide script infra/monitoring-dashboards#45).
- For cost numbers, attach the infra billing calc sheet (link to Charges tab) so finance can validate.
- If you plan to propose an action that requires engineering (e.g., change cache policy), open a short ticket (Confluence link + snoozed follow-up) and put ticket ID in the Notes column.

Playbook guidance (recommended thresholds and when to escalate):
- Latency: for self-serve tier, target p95 <= 450ms; for enterprise/dedicated, target p95 <= 250ms. If p95 exceeds tier target for two consecutive QBR windows, escalate to solutions-eng for optimization plan.
- Uptime: baseline target >=99.9% for most customers. If observed <99.8% on 30d or recurring incidents cause renewal concern, escalate to SRE and create a remediation plan with timeline.
- Cost-per-token: flag if current cost_per_1k is >20% above comparable cohort median for the same model family and workload pattern. Suggest Redwood Optimize review.
- Cache hit rate: target >=70% for workloads that are chatty or FAQ-like; if <50% for such workloads, propose cache policy reviews and A/B test.

QBR slide checklist (what CSM should present):
1) One-line summary: health + any renewal risk (green/amber/red).
2) KPI table (from above).
3) 3-month trend visual for latency and cost-per-1k.
4) Recent incidents (what changed, mitigation steps, and ownership).
5) Cost optimization opportunities and expected delta (quantified).
6) Ask / recommended next steps (engineering tickets, commit changes, pricing discussion).

Example calculations (realistic numbers):
- Latency p95 calculation snippet: collect array of request latencies for 30d -> sort -> p95 = element at index ceil(0.95*N).
- Uptime example: total_requests=1,200,000; successes=1,199,640; scheduled_maintenance_requests=360; successful_during_maintenance=360. uptime = (1,199,640 - 0) / (1,200,000 - 360) = 1,199,640 / 1,199,640 = 100% (rare but possible when maintenance served successfully).

Open questions / items to decide (for product/eng ops):
- Do we standardize on gateway_latency_ms as the single canonical latency signal even for streaming where model compute dominates? Proposal: yes, but annotate streaming latency separately.
- What is the canonical allocation technique for infra_cost for mixed shared/dedicated customers? Needs finance input (JIRA CS-915 opened).
- Should cache eligibility be surfaced in dashboards as a filterable dimension? (pro: transparency, con: dashboard complexity).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a small glossary appendix with metric IDs used in telemetry (gateway.latency.ms, serving.kv.cache.hit, billing.infra.cost).
- Draft a short email template for presenting cost opportunities to finance stakeholders.
- Build a lightweight script snippet for CSMs to generate the KPI table from dashboard exports (ask infra team for a stable API).

Revision history:
- 2025-09-15: initial draft (Priya).
- 2025-12-02: added cost allocation examples (Alex).
- 2026-02-24: clarified cache eligible definition and added playbook thresholds (Marco + Samira).

Appendix: quick reference of telemetry metric names (to be expanded):
- gateway_latency_ms (per-request)
- gateway_request_status (2xx/4xx/5xx)
- serving_kv_cache_hits
- serving_prefix_cache_hits
- billing_infra_cost_usd

Concluding note: use this doc as the canonical checklist when preparing QBR slides and renewal risk calls. Keep the customer-facing tracker minimal (the one-table format above) and put heavier math in internal attachments so customers see clear, actionable items rather than implementation noise.

End of doc.
